messages.content:
Write dense, plain prose: the most information in the fewest words. Use complete sentences. Compress related facts into coordinated clauses; attach evidence IDs in parentheses. Mention each fact once. Keep every fact, uncertainty, condition, exclusion, owner and next action. Preserve technical literals exactly. No preamble, heading, recap, generic warning or editing commentary.

Example of the desired density: "Cache expiry fell from 80 to 50 seconds; 9 tests pass (cache-run-4), but slow-client safety remains unmeasured. It is undeployed; Ren must run the slow-client staging test before release." Preserve that level of detail, without adding sentences explaining what it means.

Copy already concise sources exactly. Obey requested formats, including exact frontmatter, code blocks and JSON keys/types. Explicitly requested detail takes precedence over brevity. Check silently for lost meaning; return only the deliverable.

Draft in one normal response. Existing memo changes require an explicit rewrite request, a preview, and approved memo.write with the read expected_revision. Stop on conflict; preserve newer text and source evidence.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: reply.
Reply to a user asking why their saved edit was rejected.

Source:
The save was rejected because the document changed after the version that the user read. The user read revision r17, but revision r18 was current by the time the save reached the publication check. The system preserved the r18 text and did not overwrite it with the stale edit. The rejected edit has not been applied. This was a revision conflict, not a permission denial. The next action is to read r18, compare the intended edit with that version, and submit a new save using r18 as the expected revision if the edit still makes sense. There is no automatic retry. The diagnostic reference is save-check-9. It is not known from that diagnostic who authored r18, and the response should not guess. The user needs an explanation of the conflict and a clear next step, not a long account of implementation internals.

message.content: Your save was rejected because of a revision conflict, not a permission denial. You read revision r17, but by the time your save reached the publication check, revision r18 was current. The system preserved the r18 text and did not overwrite it with your stale edit; your rejected edit has not been applied. There is no automatic retry. To proceed, read r18, compare your intended edit against that version, and if the edit still makes sense, submit a new save using r18 as the expected revision. Diagnostic reference: save-check-9. The author of r18 is not known from that diagnostic.
